title: What DMARC Protects You From, and What It Does Not
summary: This article explains the protective capabilities of DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance) in email security, covering what it effectively protects against (domain spoofing, phishing) and its limitations (no content encryption, no protection against BEC attacks or compromised accounts).
problem_solved: Explains email domain authentication and clarifies common misconceptions about what DMARC can and cannot prevent.
why_valuable: Helps email administrators and security professionals understand realistic security boundaries of DMARC to avoid false confidence in email protection.
